sourceNotes: Window 17:40Z to 23:38Z Nov 4 (since the 12:35 run). 12 candidates (6 practical, 5 broad, 0 frontier-capital, 1 design). Post-election posts flooded the bigPicture lane; partisan items muted.

RSS: used OpenAI Blog (Pierre), MIT Tech Review (Texas data centers), The Verge (Images 2.6, as related). Simon Willison (datasette-llm alpha), Verge Qualcomm/Nothing/Musk items, Atlantic and Stratechery election pieces were off-lens or already covered. Lenny, Benedict Evans, Mollick, Gary Marcus, Hashimoto: nothing in the window.
Dwarkesh Patel RSS (dwarkeshpatel.com/feed) returns HTTP 500 again; dead for many runs now.
Metaplanet Google News: one item (planned bitcoin purchases raised after bond redemption), a capital-markets move, not a view; not used.

Hacker News (minPoints 200, AI filter): IEEE PHP2Shell (1007), Gemini training (617), RTX Spark (577), Kimi K3.1 Pro (314) were already in the 12:35 file. Ripple-65B (189) and OpenAI/Pierre (151) included below threshold as lab releases. Anthropic provable inference (162) already covered on Nov 3. Tencent Hy4 (162) page returned no readable text; not used. Residential proxies on White House network (475), AMD vs Intel (432) off-lens.
arXiv: no new batch since the 06:33 run (latest submissions Nov 3); nothing new used.

X howTo lane: @ClaudeDevs, @NousResearch used; @swyx Ripple quote and @theo Conductor quote kept as related. @gregisenberg '8 kinds of businesses' video, @kunchenguid OSS-growth list, @LangChain meetups/demo, @kloss_xyz promo, @Ronycoder ad, @poteto and @GeoffreyHuntley jokes, @theo T3 Code throughput claim (3x, no data) not used.

X bigPicture lane: @OpenAI (cyber pipeline, Images 2.6), @AnthropicAI, @AravSrinivas Decisions API used. @beffjezos, @patrickc posts were election reactions (muted). @elonmusk posts were a one-word reply and a Grok Bot plug. @a16z buyout-returns and Casado clips not used.

X frontierCapital lane: @TaviCosta silver-miners call is a market tip (excluded by contract); @RayDalio principle-of-the-day and thin @nathanbenaich quotes not used (one Benaich line quoted as a fact on Ripple). Design lane: @MengTo had no posts in the window.

Non-lane sources used because a lane voice pointed to them: @markgurman (quoted by @steipete), @charlieholtz (quoted by @theo), @perplexitydevs (quoted by @AravSrinivas), @fr0gger_ (from the queries lane).
X queries lane: mostly small-account skill listicles and promos; only the malicious-repos report cleared quality.
Replies checked on @ClaudeDevs subagent post and @OpenAI cyber post: none cleared the reply filter (>=1000 followers and >=5 likes). authorBaseline not filled this run. X calls this run: 10.

candidates.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code team says background subagents now use less of the usage limit: status-line updates every 30 seconds used to re-read the subagent's whole conversation, and are now written by Haiku 5.5 from short notes, cutting each update's cost by about 99%.
facts: Post: 'A running subagent updates its status line every 30 seconds, and each update used to re-read its whole conversation.'
Post: 'Now Haiku 5.5 writes it from short notes instead, so each update costs about 99% less.'
Announced with a video; no changelog link in the post.

candidates.summary: OpenAI says its security researchers built an autonomous pipeline that discovers, exploits and patches vulnerabilities; in a single run with an upcoming cyber model it validated and generated patches for 948 local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel at a total API cost of $1.2 million.
facts: 948 local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel validated and patched in a single run.
Total API cost stated: $1.2 million.
Uses an upcoming, unreleased cyber model.
Announced in an X post with an image; no technical write-up linked in the post, and the patches' upstream status is not stated.

related.name: IEEE Spectrum: AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt (HN 1007)

candidates.summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, a dense open-weight model it says scores 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, a new U.S. open-weight high for agentic coding, trained for a stated $32M full R&D cost and available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud and OpenRouter.
facts: Pretrained on 12 trillion tokens; up to 1M context.
Self-reported TerminalBench 2.1: 80.52, vs Reflection Beam 501B (80.1), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4), Thinking Machines Inkling 975B (63.8), NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B (56.4).
$32M is described as full R&D cost from scratch, about one-tenth of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding by the company's estimate.
Reached 80.5 with 1.4M RL rollouts, roughly 70x fewer than Reflection Beam per the company.
Says the dense 65B size runs efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.
Nathan Benaich on X: 'the whole “we’re sota for american open weight models” when you’re still worse than china is quite odd energy'.
Hacker News: 189 points.

candidates.summary: A security researcher reports finding 73 GitHub repos posing as AI agent tools (Claude skills, Codex, MCP servers, OpenClaw) that deliver malware ZIP 'installers'; 51 were still live the morning of the post.
facts: Payload: SmartLoader, a Lua loader that usually drops the StealC infostealer.
Post says the thread includes IOCs.
Single-researcher report on X (@SecurityBreakAI mentioned); not independently verified here.

candidates.summary: Nous Research unified plugins, connectors and skills for Hermes Agent into one marketplace, and opened a 7-day Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon with $20,000 in cash prizes.
facts: Marketplace: hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/marketplace.
Hackathon runs 7 days with $20,000 in cash prizes.
Post: 'A plugin can change anything from the model Hermes runs on'.

candidates.summary: Perplexity added web grounding to its Decisions API: setting "mode": "web_grounding" runs one Fast Search query per question so the pplx-decider-v1.2 model answers from the current web, for batch-mode decisions.
facts: Aravind Srinivas: search costs $0.001 per request and the Decisions API costs $0.02 per 1M input tokens.
Perplexity Developers: a decision model returns a probability but otherwise only knows its training data and your state.

candidates.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple is cutting employee AI spending budgets while pushing staff to use AI more: engineers' daily limits went from $300 to $200, with $100 planned, and some teams could fall to $25.
facts: MacRumors, citing Bloomberg: many non-engineering groups already have a $100 daily limit.
Apple is asking some teams to use cheaper models or on-device AI; employees can ask executives for more budget.
Apple lets employees use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and other models.
Some employees told Bloomberg few used their full $300 daily limit, so savings may be small.
Peter Steinberger quoting the report: 'Do individual limits still make sense?'

candidates.summary: Charlie Holtz announced that Conductor, a coding-agent app, is joining Meta to work with Nat Friedman and Alexandr Wang at Meta Superintelligence Labs on 'the next interface'.
facts: Holtz: 'I’m convinced MSL has the highest talent density of all the labs.'
Theo (T3 Code): 'T3 Code’s best competitor just joined Meta'.
Deal terms not disclosed.

candidates.summary: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, maker of Code Storage and the Trees and Diffs libraries already used in the Codex app, to build Git and code-review workflows for teams working with coding agents.
facts: Pierre's open-source projects stay open source; Code Storage customers can keep using it while features move into Codex.
OpenAI links it to Pando, its in-house source control backend for engineers and agents, shared earlier this week.
Closing is subject to regulatory approvals.
Hacker News: 151 points.

candidates.summary: Anthropic's biology lab used Claude to help map the first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells, a large protein shell of unknown function first discovered in 1986; a preprint has been submitted to bioRxiv.
facts: Claude helped search sequence literature, optimize particle isolation, and map the structure.
Anthropic: manual structure determination would have taken weeks to months; here it took days.
Anthropic says Claude made some simple mistakes that its ML researchers helped address.
Function of vaults remains unknown.

candidates.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that Texas, the fastest-growing US data center market, may slow AI buildouts after the election, as the governor-elect pushed for a data center moratorium during the campaign.
facts: On September 21 the outgoing governor directed a state regulator to halt data center permits.
Stargate Frontier in Shackelford County is projected at 1,820 MW.
Nexus Hubbard, intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 MW.
Industry panelists at DCD in Ashburn expected existing projects to slow and new ones to be halted.

related.name: The Atlantic: Silicon Valley’s Very Bad Night

candidates.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Images 2.6 with animated GIFs and reference images, and said two new image models are coming to the API with 50% faster image generation.
facts: Features: GIFs and reference images.
Two new API models, 50% faster image generation (per OpenAI).
The Verge covered the GIF feature the same day.
